description: Delineation of Total Impact Zones of Potential Landslides based on Red and Yellow Zone Methodology
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-10-21 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that the mountainous area, which constitutes about 30% of the total land area of ​​the country spreading over 14 districts, is at risk of landslides. Landslide hazard zonation maps are developed and utilized by the National Building Research Organization as a primary tool for the early identification of landslide-prone slopes of hills and their distribution. Accordingly, landslide hazard zone maps had been prepared covering most of the landslide-prone areas in Sri Lanka by the year 2023. Such zone maps only indicate areas, susceptible for landslide initiations. However, in landslide risk management, it is essential to identify the entire area that may be affected by a landslide, including the landslide initiation zone, debris flow path and depositional areas. Recognizing that situation, the National Building Research Organization has proposed a project titled 'Delineation of Total Impact Zones of Potential Landslides based on Red and Yellow Zone Methodology'. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Defence to implement the said project, taking into account the urgent need to minimize the risk of landslide disasters in the island, was approved by the Cabinet.
